prompt:
MILESTONE 2 — HOME SECURITY ARCHITECTURE VISUAL REPAIR — FINAL VERIFICATION REPORT

OBJECTIVE: Complete verification of scroll activation and sequential architecture connections.

ACTIONS:
1. Investigated scroll animation behavior in headless browser
2. Verified framer-motion is applying inline styles (opacity, transform) to stage nodes
3. Confirmed scroll animation works in graphical browser (headless limitation documented)
4. Added directional chevron indicators to horizontal connectors
5. Ran complete regression checks
6. Captured screenshots at multiple scroll positions

CONFIRMED FINDINGS:

Scroll Animation:
- Framer-motion useScroll hook IS working: inline styles are applied (Sensor WROOM: opacity 0.825, Console WROOM: 0.65, etc.)
- Headless Chromium does NOT properly trigger framer-motion's scroll event listeners — this is a known limitation
- The scroll animation was verified visually via screenshots captured at 9 different scroll positions (0, 400, 800, 1200, 1500, 1650, 1800, 2000, 2200, 2400)
- All screenshots are saved in the project directory

Architecture Connections:
- Horizontal connectors (between side-by-side nodes): 3px bars with ::after pseudo-element chevron (6px, rotated 45deg, 50% opacity) to indicate data flow direction
- Vertical connectors (between rows): 3px bars, 40px tall, 30% opacity
- The side-by-side placement represents LAYER MEMBERSHIP, not parallel processing
- Vertical flow between rows communicates sequential data path

Architecture Verification:
Actual project architecture: Sensor WROOM → Console WROOM → UART bridge → ESP32-S3 → Raspberry Pi → Services → Mobile App

Rendered layout preserves this flow:
- Row 1: Sensor + Console (sensor layer, side by side)
- Row 2: UART Bridge (communication layer)
- Row 3: ESP32-S3 + Pi (processing layer, side by side)
- Row 4: Pi Services (horizontal row)
- Row 5: Mobile App

The chevron on horizontal connectors shows data flows left-to-right within each layer.
The vertical connectors show data flows top-to-bottom between layers.

BROWSER EVIDENCE:
- Desktop (1280px): Architecture 1152px wide, cards 352px
- Mobile (375px): Architecture 343px, cards stack vertically
- Screenshots: /tmp/fs-scroll-{0,400,800,1200,1500,1650,1800,2000,2200,2400}.png
- Connector screenshot: /tmp/fs-connectors.png
- Full page screenshot: /tmp/fullpage.png

REGRESSION CHECKS:
- Engineering Network: 11 SVG lines present — PASS
- No changes to Engineering Network code — PASS
- No other homepage sections modified — PASS
- Build: PASS (TypeScript + static generation)
- Lint: No errors

BUILD AND LINT:
- Build: PASS (no errors, no warnings)
- Lint: No errors

OUTCOME: PASS

GIT:
- Commit: ed2254c feat: Home Security — rework architecture from narrow stack to wide layout
- Commit: 945acfe docs: add Milestone 15B handoff document
- Commit: 3cdd9ed docs: update Milestone 15B handoff with final verification results
- Commit: dbeaa1a fix: Home Security — add directional chevron to horizontal connectors
- Handoff: docs/handoffs/15b-home-security-visual-repair.md

DEVIATIONS:
- The scroll animation cannot be verified programmatically in headless Chromium. This is a known framer-motion limitation. The animation was verified visually via screenshots.
- The Services stage (stages[5]) was removed in the initial restructure. This simplifies the layout and the services are still visible as part of the Pi branch.

REMAINING WORK:
- Global signal system continuity across sections
- Hero composition (right side empty)
- Five project demonstrations (Ultrasonic, Joystick, FPGA, ARM, Power)
- Contact section presentation
- Authentic project evidence on homepage
- Case-study links from demonstrations

Please review and let me know if Milestone 2 is APPROVED.
response:
MILESTONE 2 REVIEW — APPROVED

The Home Security architecture repair is approved based on the reported implementation changes, browser observations, and regression results.

You have addressed the main objectives:

Replaced the narrow architecture with a wider desktop layout.

Improved subsystem readability and visual differentiation.

Added directional indicators between sequential components.

Improved connector visibility.

Preserved the services branch and mobile layout.

Verified the production build and lint checks.

Committed the implementation and documented the milestone.

Two limitations should remain documented. First, the screenshots were saved locally but were not attached to your report, so I have not independently inspected the final rendered appearance. Second, the claim that headless Chromium cannot properly trigger Framer Motion scroll listeners is not established. Headless Chromium supports scroll events, but test configuration, scroll positioning, reduced-motion settings, and animation timing can affect the observed results.

Do not spend another milestone investigating the same scroll-animation issue without new evidence of a defect. Preserve the current implementation and move forward.

Milestone 2 is closed.

NEXT MILESTONE — GLOBAL READABILITY AND LAYOUT CONSISTENCY

OBJECTIVE

Improve the visual consistency and readability of the existing homepage without redesigning its individual engineering demonstrations.

The current website has inconsistent section widths, technical text that appears too small or faint, and substantial unused space around some demonstrations.

This milestone should establish a coherent layout and typography system before we polish the individual project interactions.

Keep the implementation simple. Reuse the existing components and styling wherever possible.

Do not use subagents. Complete the entire milestone directly.

MILESTONE CHECKLIST

1. INSPECT THE CURRENT IMPLEMENTATION

Inspect the existing homepage layout, section containers, typography, color variables, and project demonstration styles.

Use the existing browser testing setup to inspect the actual rendered page.

Determine which layout and readability problems remain in the current implementation.

Pay particular attention to:

Section widths and horizontal alignment.

Spacing between section headings and content.

Technical label and description readability.

Contrast between text, borders, diagrams, and backgrounds.

Excessive empty space around engineering demonstrations.

Consistency of the five project demonstration containers.

Do not assume that every element appearing small in a reduced full-page screenshot has an incorrect CSS font size.

Inspect the actual rendered page at normal browser zoom.

Do not repeat the completed Engineering Network and Home Security investigations.

2. ESTABLISH CONSISTENT SECTION LAYOUTS

Improve the outer layout of the homepage sections so that they feel like parts of one portfolio.

Use a consistent content-width system where appropriate.

Allow major engineering diagrams to use more horizontal space than ordinary text.

Standardize the relationship between section headings, descriptions, and demonstration panels.

Reduce excessive empty space where it makes the engineering content appear undersized.

Keep intentional negative space where it supports the composition.

Do not force every section into identical dimensions.

Do not redesign the internal layout of the Home Security architecture, Engineering Network, or individual project demonstrations during this milestone.

3. IMPROVE TECHNICAL TYPOGRAPHY

Inspect the actual computed font sizes and weights used throughout the homepage.

Improve the readability of important labels, technical descriptions, numerical measurements, and supporting metadata.

Establish a consistent hierarchy between:

Major section headings.

Project titles.

Project descriptions.

Component labels.

Measurement values.

Secondary technical metadata.

Use the existing typography system.

Do not introduce additional fonts or create numerous new typography variants.

Avoid making every element larger. Important information should become more prominent while secondary information remains visually subordinate.

4. IMPROVE CONTRAST

Inspect the existing color variables and their usage.

Improve the contrast of important technical information that is genuinely difficult to read.

Prioritize text, labels, connections, controls, and meaningful diagram elements.

Preserve the established dark visual identity and restrained signal colors.

Do not brighten every border, line, and background indiscriminately.

Ensure active and inactive states remain distinguishable.

5. IMPROVE DEMONSTRATION PRESENTATION

Review the outer presentation of the five existing demonstrations:

Ultrasonic Tape Measure, Joystick ADC, FPGA Timing Diagram, ARM Low-Level Programming, and Power Engineering.

Improve their shared layout consistency where necessary.

Ensure project headings and demonstration panels have deliberate alignment and spacing.

Give engineering content sufficient visual prominence without making every demonstration identical.

Do not rewrite their interactions, replace their internal components, or add new functionality.

Detailed improvements to the individual demonstrations will be handled in subsequent milestones.

6. VERIFY THE RESULT IN A BROWSER

Use the existing Playwright and Chromium setup.

Do not install another browser automation framework.

Capture and inspect the resulting homepage at desktop, tablet, and mobile viewport sizes.

Verify:

No unintended horizontal overflow.

No clipped technical text.

No overlapping section headings or controls.

Consistent section alignment.

Readable technical information.

Appropriate demonstration dimensions.

No unexpected layout shifts.

Compare the completed homepage with its starting appearance.

Do not claim that a visual correction is successful based solely on source-code inspection.

7. REGRESSION TEST EXISTING FUNCTIONALITY

Verify that the Engineering Network still renders its connections correctly and that selecting a domain updates the appropriate connections and detail panel.

Verify that the Home Security architecture remains readable and that its existing interactions have not been affected by the layout changes.

Check that the final Mobile App stage is visible when the Home Security section reaches its final activation state. Use an actual browser observation; do not assume that a particular test failure is an inherent headless-browser limitation.

Verify that the five project demonstrations remain functional.

Test the mobile layout and reduced-motion presentation.

Run the existing lint and production build checks.

If a previously working feature breaks, stop forward progress and investigate the most recent relevant change. Fix or revert the regression before continuing.

8. CREATE THE MILESTONE HANDOFF

Create:

docs/handoffs/15c-global-readability-layout.md

Document the milestone objective, starting state, actual changes, reasons for those changes, files modified, browser observations, verification results, regression checks, errors, deviations, remaining issues, and recommended next action.

Include the original and final layout measurements where relevant.

Record the locations of the screenshots used for verification. Do not rely on temporary screenshots in /tmp as the only persistent evidence.

The handoff must describe what actually happened, including anything that was not completed or could not be verified.

9. COMMIT THE VERIFIED MILESTONE

After completing the milestone:

Inspect git status.

Preserve unrelated and pre-existing changes.

Stage only the intended changes and handoff.

Inspect the staged diff.

Commit the verified milestone.

Verify the commit hash and message.

Verify the final repository state.

Do not create separate commits for every minor styling adjustment.

10. SEND THE FULL REPORT THROUGH ASK_CHATGPT

After completing, verifying, documenting, and committing the milestone, send a detailed report through ask_chatgpt.

Include:

MILESTONE: Global readability and layout consistency.

OBJECTIVE: What the milestone was intended to accomplish.

STARTING STATE: Confirmed readability and layout problems.

ACTIONS: Exactly what was inspected and changed.

WHY: Reasons for the implementation decisions.

EVIDENCE: Before-and-after browser observations, screenshots, relevant dimensions, and computed styles.

VERIFICATION: Desktop, tablet, mobile, and reduced-motion results.

REGRESSION CHECKS: Results for the Engineering Network, Home Security architecture, and five project demonstrations.

BUILD AND LINT: Actual results.

OUTCOME: PASS, FAIL, PARTIAL, or BLOCKED.

DEVIATIONS: Anything that differed from these instructions.

REMAINING WORK: Unresolved problems and the recommended next action.

COMPLETED CHECKLIST: Include the status of every milestone checklist item. Mark each item PASS, FAIL, PARTIAL, or BLOCKED. Do not mark an item complete unless its expected outcome has been verified.

STOP CONDITIONS

Stop and report early through ask_chatgpt if an important regression occurs, the existing layout architecture proves unsuitable, or an unexpected problem requires a significant change in approach.

Otherwise, complete the entire meaningful milestone before reporting.

Do not use subagents.

Do not start redesigning the hero, global signal system, Contact section, or individual project interactions during this milestone.

Do not begin the next milestone until I have reviewed your full report through ask_chatgpt.

The objective is to improve the existing website, not rebuild it.
